result.title: Grokking as a Subspace Search: Computing the Destination Before Training
result.summary: Grokking is the phenomenon in which a neural network generalizes long after it has memorized its training data. Many explanations have been proposed for the delay between memorization and generalization. However, none of them can say before training where the network is heading, so they cannot be tested against one another. We show that on group tasks this destination can be computed from the task itself before training begins. It is a low-dimensional subspace of the network's embeddings, which we call the right subspace, and we prove that it is essentially unique. Knowing the destination makes our hypothesis falsifiable: the delay is a search for the right subspace, and generalization begins when the network finds it. When we give the network the right subspace from the start, the delay disappears. When we take the right subspace away, accuracy stops at a ceiling that we compute before training, and on multiplication the network cannot generalize at all. When we train the network normally, its embeddings move toward the right subspace by themselves, long before test accuracy rises. Finally, interventions during training show that this search sets the length of the delay, and that noise in the optimization does not. On every group task that we tested, grokking is a search for the right subspace, and the delay is the time that this search takes.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究 grokking 现象：在群任务上，从任务本身即可在训练前算出泛化所对应的低维嵌入子空间「right subspace」，并证明其基本唯一；通过训练前注入、移除该子空间及训练中干预，验证泛化延迟等于网络搜索到该子空间所需时间。
AI.relevance_reason: 「表示子空间可由任务预先计算、延迟即搜索该子空间的时间」这一框架，可能为 LVR 中 latent 状态是否收敛到任务决定的低维结构、动态计算与训练长度预算的因果解释提供可核查的类比，但任务限于群运算，与视觉推理的关联需阅读原文判断。
